note: Hand-kept from news reports found by the Deep South probe (tools/probe_dsources.mjs, PROBE_SET=peace) and the tab's own peace-talk reports. Every line is what an official, a party or an outlet said: claims, not findings. Add new lines at the top of rounds, with their sources, and rebuild with node tools/build_deepsouth_peace.mjs.

status.short: Stalled since the Kuala Lumpur technical talks of 4 July 2026; no new date found in reporting.
status.summary: Stalled. The last talks reported were technical talks in Kuala Lumpur on 4 July 2026; a September round was called off after attacks in July, and by mid-September outlets reported the talks stalled. Both sides have since signalled interest in renewed talks; no new date has been found in reporting.

parties.name: Thai government peace dialogue panel
parties.note: Led since May 2026 by Thanut Suvarnananda, director of the National Intelligence Agency, appointed chief of peace dialogue by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.

parties.name: Barisan Revolusi Nasional Melayu Patani (BRN)
parties.role: Main insurgent group at the table
parties.note: Speaks through its Peace Dialogue Secretariat. Says negotiation is the best route to a political solution and that its armed wing follows international humanitarian law (its claim).

parties.name: Malaysia
parties.note: Facilitator Mohd Rabin Basir, a former chief of Malaysia's National Security Council. Malaysia pledged full cooperation with the new Thai chief negotiator in July 2026.

parties.name: Other Patani groups (PULO, MARA Patani)
parties.note: The Thai chief negotiator said he also wants to talk with other groups; BRN rejected a proposal to bring other groups into the dialogue.

rounds.what: Amid new attacks, militants and Thai officials signal interest in renewed peace talks.
BRN rejects a proposal to bring other liberation groups into the dialogue with the Thai government.
BRN says it will keep fighting for self-determination as the talks stall.
The Thai government rejects autonomy and independence for the three provinces and says it is ready to offer other forms of administration.
Malaysia tightens security on its land border with Thailand after the attacks and says it will appoint facilitators for the talks.
After more than 70 incidents over one weekend, officials say talks with BRN may still be held in September.
The chief negotiator tells Reuters Thailand is ready to change its approach and revive the peace process.
The September round is called off after the Narathiwat attack that killed five rangers; talks postponed indefinitely.
The Prime Minister says talks with BRN will continue despite a car bombing.
Malaysia pledges full cooperation with the new Thai chief negotiator; its facilitator stays in the role.
BRN says it is still committed to the process and blames slow progress for the rise in violence; the Thai negotiator says a BRN statement issued during the talks disrupted them.
Technical talks between Thailand and BRN, with Malaysia as facilitator.
The chief negotiator plans more public participation, bringing residents and young people into direct dialogue with BRN.
The new chief negotiator meets 47 civil society groups; stalled talks are reported set to resume in Kuala Lumpur that week.
The Prime Minister's chief adviser says talks will resume in late June after a two-year pause, following a meeting with Malaysia's ambassador.
Background: after two days of talks, the Thai delegation and BRN agree in principle on the Joint Comprehensive Plan toward Peace (JCPP), to be endorsed at the earliest opportunity.
